brief.headline: fcf3261e135d: raise inside for-loop fires on first iteration miss, skipping remaining candidates

sentences.text: Commit fcf3261e135d introduced a for-loop over three candidate forms of an order id, but placed the raise LookupError inside the loop body at the same indentation level as the return.
This means the loop raises on the very first iteration that does not match, instead of trying all three forms and only raising after exhausting them.

Because the loop iterates a set, the order of the three candidates is non-deterministic, so the plain order_id form is not always tried first, making the failure intermittent and explaining the ~39% failure rate.
In the failing run, lookup_order was called with order_id '1002', which exists in ORDERS, but the tool returned a 404 error instead of the record.
In the passing run at the parent commit, the same input '1002' was resolved immediately and the refund completed successfully.
The fix is to dedent the raise so it is outside the for-loop, executing only after all candidate keys have been tried.
